selectionReason: RC62 left a frozen local-ladder influence audit as the most direct gate before opening early-universe models. The official SH0ES compact release makes the numerical fit immediately reproducible, while its ability to support the promised named interventions could be decided without new telescope time.
newVerifiedFacts: Six official SH0ES release files totaling 49,462,230 bytes were frozen at commit c447f0fea703fcd0fff57de5000947b5ca81286b; every byte count and SHA-256 matches the manifest.
The released system contains 3,492 observations, 47 parameters, and a symmetric positive-definite covariance matrix; the design has full column rank.
A covariance-whitened QR fit gives H0=73.0428191+-1.0071479 km/s/Mpc, reproducing the published 73.04+-1.04 within the preregistered 0.05 tolerances.

The official lstsq_results vector differs by as much as 0.04962 in a parameter, failing the preregistered 0.0005 comparison; the official README identifies that file as a constructor for a broad initial prior rather than a precision posterior reference.
The FITS headers provide array dimensions and 2021 creation dates but no row identities, parameter names, anchor, host, instrument, filter, method, or covariance-ancestry map.
The compact matrix predates the 2024 SMC anchor result and the 2024-2025 JWST common-host results, so it cannot execute those branches even if its older rows were labelled.
Among 3,491 identifiable single-row deletions, the largest anonymous H0 displacement is 0.30414 baseline sigma; one row uniquely constrains a parameter and makes the reduced system non-identifiable.

Exact covariance-preserving deletion of 86 anonymous design-signature blocks leaves 83 identifiable fits; the largest H0 displacement is 0.67914 baseline sigma and no identifiable block crosses one sigma.
A dependency-free Node solve agrees with Python within 1.7e-12 in H0, 4.5e-11 across parameters, and 8.8e-11 in the seven identifiable constraint-row deletions.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The public 2022 compact system is sufficient to reproduce its published numerical H0 baseline.
The compact system supports named leave-one-anchor, host, photometric-system, and HST-versus-JWST causal estimates.
No one identifiable row or design-signature block moves H0 by one baseline sigma in the released system.
A second implementation reproduces the fit and anonymous constraint deletions within the frozen numerical tolerances.
A current, fully labelled HST-JWST-SMC release will keep every named branch below one sigma under covariance-preserving deletion.

causalChain: Input: exact y, L, and C arrays frozen from the official SH0ES commit, plus a published H0 target used only as a reproduction check.
Bottleneck: numerical rows cannot be assigned to astrophysical anchors, hosts, instruments, or covariance ancestors from the released metadata.
Bridge: a complete semantic release contract maps every row, parameter, and covariance component to stable identities and current measurement branches.
Adjudicand: independently reproduced H0 shifts from covariance-preserving named deletions and held common-host residuals.
Resolution: the required-ruler discrepancy survives every current named branch deletion below one sigma and is then tested by an early-universe model against full CMB, BBN, and growth data.

workPackages.purpose: Obtain or construct a semantically complete current ladder release.
workPackages.method: Request or publish row and parameter dictionaries, covariance-component ancestry, selection recipes, and HST-JWST-SMC branch identifiers conforming to the RC63 contract.
workPackages.deliverable: Versioned current y-L-C arrays plus validated observation, parameter, covariance, and intervention tables.
workPackages.pass: Every row and parameter is labelled, every covariance component has ancestry, and all current branches are represented.
workPackages.fail: Any identity is inferred only from matrix position, a covariance component cannot be rebuilt, or current branches remain absent.
workPackages.next: If failed, retain only the anonymous influence envelope and do not attribute a shift to an anchor or instrument.

workPackages.purpose: Execute the frozen named local-ladder influence audit.
workPackages.method: For each anchor, calibrator host, photometric system, and method branch, remove its observations and descended covariance components, refit, and adjudicate on independently coded fits and held common-host residuals.
workPackages.deliverable: Named H0 influence table with branch-specific uncertainty, residual score, and covariance rebuild receipt.
workPackages.pass: No named branch moves H0 by one full-fit sigma and held residuals show no boundary-aligned failure.
workPackages.fail: A branch crosses one sigma, loses identifiability, or disagrees between implementations beyond tolerance.
workPackages.next: If failed, make that measurement branch the active calibration problem and keep early-universe grids closed.

workPackages.purpose: Separate release semantics from cosmological model flexibility.
workPackages.method: Only after W2 passes, combine the family-conditioned 132.8-136.1 Mpc ruler envelope with preregistered early-energy, extra-radiation, and recombination predictions for full CMB, BBN, matter power, and growth.
workPackages.pass: One physical model reaches every surviving ruler interval without violating any held observable or using post-outcome nuisance tuning.
workPackages.fail: The model reaches only selected families, breaks held data, or requires opening additional freedom after seeing the result.
workPackages.next: If all declared families fail, publish the excluded region and return to the measured calibration branch rather than adding unrestricted parameters.

uncertaintyBudget: Numerical: float32 released arrays are solved in float64; QR and independent partial-pivot elimination agree far below the frozen tolerance.
Measurement: the compact covariance carries the 2022 modelled uncertainties, but this cycle does not regenerate photometry, crowding corrections, artificial-star tests, or selection effects.
Semantic: row and parameter identities are absent, so anonymous structure must not be translated into a named anchor or instrument.
Temporal: 2024 SMC and 2024-2025 JWST results postdate the compact arrays and cannot be represented by deletions from them.
Intervention: slicing rows is valid only with matching covariance ancestry; alternative selections may require new artificial-star uncertainty characterization as the official release warns.
External validity: a sub-one-sigma anonymous deletion envelope in the 2022 linear system does not prove stability of the current ladder.
structuralConnection: CONN-EVIDENCE-036 links cosmological calibration influence to identifiability under interventions: a numerically invertible model can still make a named causal question unidentifiable when observation identity and covariance ancestry are missing.
failedOrRejectedAttempts: The preregistered comparison with lstsq_results failed by 0.04962 because that official file is an initial broad-prior constructor, not a precision posterior target; the failed gate is preserved rather than retuned.
A named MW, LMC, NGC 4258, host, photometric-system, or HST-JWST effect could not be calculated without guessing identities from design columns, so the analysis stopped at anonymous rows and blocks.
One single-row deletion made a parameter unidentifiable; it is reported as non-identifiable instead of receiving a pseudoinverse H0 value.
The 2022 matrix could not represent the later SMC and JWST branches, preventing the current full-ladder stability claim.
claimBoundary: RC63 reproduces the released 2022 linear baseline and exact anonymous deletion envelopes. It does not identify an astrophysical anchor from a matrix column, validate the current HST-JWST-SMC ladder, solve the Hubble tension, or establish early-universe physics.
exactNextStart: Acquire a current row dictionary, parameter dictionary, covariance-component ancestry, and HST-JWST-SMC branch matrices satisfying rc63-shoes-semantic-release-contract.json. Validate named deletion fixtures before viewing H0 shifts, then run leave-one-anchor, host, photometric-system, and common-host HST-versus-JWST tests. Keep the early-universe grid closed unless every named branch stays below one full-fit sigma.
